description: Mutable State (M10) - mut/set! bindings, auto-boxed mutable closure capture, box and atom containers with deref/reset!/swap! builtins.

userStories.title: Foundation: JaclMutableRef, value tags, and compiler is_mutable tracking
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the value-level and compiler-level infrastructure for mutable state so that subsequent stories can build on it.
acceptanceCriteria: Add JACL_TAG_CELL (0x0A), JACL_TAG_BOX (0x0B), JACL_TAG_ATOM (0x0C) to value.c as new type tags
Add JaclMutableRef struct in value.c: typedef struct { JaclVal value; } JaclMutableRef — shared by cell, box, and atom
Add constructor jacl_cell_ptr(JaclMutableRef*) that returns JACL_TAG_CELL | pointer, and jacl_as_cell(JaclVal) that extracts JaclMutableRef*
Add jacl_is_cell(JaclVal) predicate that checks type tag == JACL_TAG_CELL
Add same constructor/accessor/predicate for box (jacl_box_ptr, jacl_as_box, jacl_is_box) and atom (jacl_atom_ptr, jacl_as_atom, jacl_is_atom)
Add bool is_mutable field to the Local struct in compiler.c (default false)
Add bool is_mutable field to the GlobalArity struct in compiler.c (default false)
Add bool is_mutable field to the Upvalue struct in compiler.c (default false)

Add new opcodes to bytecode.c enum (before OP_HALT): OP_MAKE_CELL, OP_GET_CELL_LOCAL, OP_SET_CELL_LOCAL, OP_GET_CELL_UPVALUE, OP_SET_CELL_UPVALUE, OP_SET_GLOBAL, OP_BOX, OP_ATOM, OP_DEREF, OP_RESET, OP_SWAP, OP_IS_BOX, OP_IS_ATOM
Update test_bytecode.c test_opcode_enum for shifted OP_HALT value
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: All 3 tags (cell/box/atom) use the same JaclMutableRef struct. Only the tag differs. Cell is internal (auto-boxing), box and atom are user-facing. The ! character is already valid in JACL words (set!, reset!, swap! will tokenize as single tokens).

userStories.title: mut — mutable local bindings with cell auto-boxing
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to declare mutable local variables with mut so that I can update their values later with set!.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'mut' as a special form in compiler__compile_command() (same pattern as 'def')
Arity check: mut requires exactly 2 arguments (name + value); compile error otherwise
At local scope (scope_depth > 0): compile RHS, emit OP_MAKE_CELL, add local with is_mutable=true, emit OP_NIL (mut returns nil)
OP_MAKE_CELL VM handler: pop value, allocate JaclMutableRef on arena, set ref->value = popped value, push jacl_cell_ptr(ref)
When reading a mut local via $x (AST_VAR_REF), compiler emits OP_GET_CELL_LOCAL instead of OP_GET_LOCAL
OP_GET_CELL_LOCAL VM handler (uint8_t slot operand): read cell from vm->stack[frame->stack_base + slot], extract JaclMutableRef* via jacl_as_cell(), push ref->value
compiler__resolve_local() returns is_mutable info so the caller knows which opcode to emit — either via out-param or by checking locals[i].is_mutable after resolve
[mut x 42] returns nil (like def)
mut can shadow existing bindings in the same or enclosing scope
Create test/jacl/mut_local_basic.jacl: mut x 42, print $x => 42; mut y 0, print $y => 0
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: All mut locals are auto-boxed into cells, even if never captured by a closure. This simplifies the single-pass compiler. The overhead is one arena allocation per mut local. Optimization to only box captured locals can be done later.

userStories.title: set! — reassign mutable locals with compile-time immutability checks
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to reassign a mutable local variable with set! and get a compile-time error if I try to mutate a def binding or parameter.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'set!' as a special form in compiler__compile_command()
Arity check: set! requires exactly 2 arguments (name + value); compile error otherwise
set! is a special form: first argument is a bare name (not $name), second is an expression
set! resolves name via compiler__resolve_local first — if found and is_mutable, compile RHS then emit OP_SET_CELL_LOCAL
OP_SET_CELL_LOCAL VM handler (uint8_t slot operand): pop new value from stack, read cell from local slot, extract JaclMutableRef* via jacl_as_cell(), store new value in ref->value, push JACL_NIL
Compile-time error if set! targets a def local: 'cannot mutate immutable binding <name>'
Compile-time error if set! targets a function parameter: 'cannot mutate parameter <name>'
Compile-time error if set! targets an undeclared name (not found as local, upvalue, or global): 'undefined variable <name>'
[set! x 99] returns nil
set! works with expressions: [set! x [+ $x 1]] increments x
Create test/jacl/set_local.jacl: mut x 0, set! x 42, print $x => 42; mut y 10, set! y [+ $y 5], print $y => 15
Create test/jacl/set_immutable_error.jacl with # expect-error: testing set! on def binding
Create test/jacl/set_param_error.jacl with # expect-error: testing set! on function parameter
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: set! only resolves locals in this story. Upvalue and global resolution is added in US-004 and US-005. When resolve_local fails, the story should fall through to upvalue and global checks (which will error for now until those stories are implemented).

userStories.title: mut/set! for mutable globals
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to declare and reassign mutable global variables so that top-level state can be updated.
acceptanceCriteria: mut at global scope (scope_depth == 0) emits OP_DEF_GLOBAL and records the name as mutable in the compiler's GlobalArity (or GlobalInfo) array with is_mutable=true
set! resolves globals after local and upvalue lookup fails: if name found in global info and is_mutable, compile RHS then emit OP_SET_GLOBAL
OP_SET_GLOBAL VM handler (uint16_t name_index operand): pop value, read name from constant pool, call vm__env_set(vm, name, value), push JACL_NIL
Compile-time error: set! on a global declared with def: 'cannot mutate immutable binding <name>'
Multiple set! on the same mutable global works correctly
Global mut does NOT use cells (globals are already in a name->value lookup table, no indirection needed)
Create test/jacl/mut_global.jacl: mut counter 0, set! counter 1, set! counter [+ $counter 1], print $counter => 2
Create test/jacl/set_global_immutable_error.jacl with # expect-error: testing set! on def global
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: The GlobalArity struct already tracks global names and arity info. Adding is_mutable to it is straightforward. The compiler's global tracking functions (compiler__resolve_global_arity etc.) need to propagate the is_mutable flag.

userStories.title: Mutable closure capture — shared mutation via cells
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want closures that capture mut variables to share mutations with the enclosing scope so that closures can be used for stateful patterns like counters and accumulators.
acceptanceCriteria: When resolve_upvalue finds a mut local in the enclosing scope, the Upvalue struct's is_mutable flag is set to true
is_mutable propagates through transitive upvalue capture (inner closure capturing from parent which captured from grandparent)
When reading a mut upvalue via $x, compiler emits OP_GET_CELL_UPVALUE instead of OP_GET_UPVALUE
OP_GET_CELL_UPVALUE VM handler (uint8_t index operand): read cell from frame->closure->upvalues[index], extract JaclMutableRef* via jacl_as_cell(), push ref->value
When set! targets a mut upvalue, compiler emits OP_SET_CELL_UPVALUE

OP_SET_CELL_UPVALUE VM handler (uint8_t index operand): pop new value, read cell from frame->closure->upvalues[index], extract JaclMutableRef* via jacl_as_cell(), store new value in ref->value, push JACL_NIL
OP_CLOSURE capture logic unchanged: cell JaclVal is copied by value from local slot or parent upvalue into closure's upvalue array (both now point to the same heap cell)
Mutation in closure visible in enclosing scope: mut x 0; proc inc { set! x [+ $x 1] }; [inc]; print $x => 1
Mutation in enclosing scope visible in closure: mut x 0; proc get-x { $x }; set! x 42; print [get-x] => 42
Multiple closures sharing the same mut local all see each other's mutations
Transitive capture: inner closure captures mut from grandparent scope through parent
Create test/jacl/mut_closure_shared.jacl with counter pattern: mut n 0, proc inc { set! n [+ $n 1] }, proc get { $n }, [inc], [inc], print [get] => 2
Create test/jacl/mut_closure_bidirectional.jacl: mutation visible in both directions
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: The existing OP_CLOSURE handler copies upvalue JaclVals by value. Since mut locals are cells (heap pointers), copying the cell JaclVal means both the enclosing scope's local slot and the closure's upvalue slot point to the same JaclMutableRef on the heap. No changes needed to OP_CLOSURE itself.

userStories.title: box and atom container constructors and type predicates
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want box (thread-local mutable container) and atom (CAS container) so that I can create first-class mutable references to pass around.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'box' as a builtin (1 arg): compile arg, emit OP_BOX
OP_BOX VM handler: pop value, check jacl_is_error (propagate if error), allocate JaclMutableRef on arena, set ref->value = value, push jacl_box_ptr(ref)
Compiler recognizes 'atom' as a builtin (1 arg): compile arg, emit OP_ATOM
OP_ATOM VM handler: pop value, check jacl_is_error (propagate if error), allocate JaclMutableRef on arena, set ref->value = value, push jacl_atom_ptr(ref)
Compiler recognizes 'box?' as a builtin (1 arg): compile arg, emit OP_IS_BOX
OP_IS_BOX VM handler: pop value, push JACL_TRUE if jacl_is_box(value), else JACL_FALSE
Compiler recognizes 'atom?' as a builtin (1 arg): compile arg, emit OP_IS_ATOM
OP_IS_ATOM VM handler: pop value, push JACL_TRUE if jacl_is_atom(value), else JACL_FALSE
[box 42] creates a box; [box? [box 42]] => $true; [box? 42] => $false
[atom 0] creates an atom; [atom? [atom 0]] => $true; [atom? 0] => $false
Error propagation: [box [error 'x']] returns the error, does not create a box
Create test/jacl/box_create.jacl and test/jacl/atom_create.jacl with creation and predicate tests
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: In M10, atom is functionally identical to box at runtime. CAS semantics are added in M13 (Concurrency). The ! character is already valid in JACL words (lexer__is_word_char allows it).

userStories.title: deref, reset!, swap! builtins for box and atom containers
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want builtins to read and update the values inside box and atom containers.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'deref' as a builtin (1 arg): compile arg, emit OP_DEREF
OP_DEREF VM handler: pop container, if error-flagged push error back; if not box or atom, push error 'deref: expected box or atom'; else extract JaclMutableRef* and push ref->value
Compiler recognizes 'reset!' as a builtin (2 args): compile container arg, compile value arg, emit OP_RESET

OP_RESET VM handler: pop new-value + container; if either error-flagged, push first error; if container not box/atom, push error 'reset!: expected box or atom'; else store new-value in ref->value, push new-value (returns the new value)
Compiler recognizes 'swap!' as a builtin (2 args): compile container arg, compile closure arg, emit OP_SWAP

OP_SWAP VM handler: pop closure + container; if either error-flagged, push first error; if container not box/atom, push error; if closure not a closure, push error; else read current ref->value, push closure, push current value as arg, call via OP_CALL mechanism, on return store result in ref->value, push result
[deref [box 42]] returns 42
[reset! [box 0] 99] returns 99; subsequent deref returns 99
def b [box 0]; [swap! $b [proc {x} { [+ $x 1] }]]; print [deref $b] => 1
swap! works on both box and atom
Runtime error: [deref 42] => error with message 'deref: expected box or atom'
Runtime error: [reset! 42 99] => error with message
Error propagation: [deref [error 'x']] returns the error unchanged
Create test/jacl/deref_basic.jacl, test/jacl/reset_basic.jacl, test/jacl/swap_basic.jacl
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: OP_SWAP is the most complex opcode — it needs to invoke the closure using the VM's existing call frame machinery. The simplest approach: push closure and arg on stack, set up a CallFrame (like OP_CALL does), call vm__run(vm, current_frame_count) to execute, then read the return value from the stack, store in ref->value, and push result. Follow the same pattern as OP_EACH/OP_TRANSFORM/OP_FILTER for inline closure calls.

userStories.title: Update print for box, atom, and cell types
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want print to display box and atom values with meaningful formatting, while cells remain transparent.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_PRINT handler updated: if value is JACL_TAG_BOX, format as '<box: VALUE>' where VALUE is the contained ref->value formatted recursively
OP_PRINT handler updated: if value is JACL_TAG_ATOM, format as '<atom: VALUE>' where VALUE is the contained ref->value formatted recursively
OP_PRINT handler: JACL_TAG_CELL is transparent — dereference the cell and print the contained value directly (user never sees '<cell: ...>')
vm__fmt_value (VMFormatBuf formatter) also updated for the new types (used by to-string and nested formatting)
Nested containers: [print [box [vec 1 2 3]]] outputs '<box: [1 2 3]>'
[print [atom 42]] outputs '<atom: 42>'
No regression on existing print behavior for all other types
Create test/jacl/print_box_atom.jacl with print output tests
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: Cell transparency in print: when OP_PRINT encounters a cell-tagged value, it should dereference it and print the inner value. This matches the user-facing behavior where cells are invisible. The vm__fmt_value function should do the same for to-string and nested formatting contexts.
